notes: Only rights-cleared, no-download entries appear in the playable collection. Destinations are official releases, publisher-released freeware/shareware, open-source projects, or pages hosted by the Internet Archive under its own preservation/takedown policies. We host no game files, ROMs, BIOS files or assets. Links were verified reachable on 2 Nov 2026; the authoring sandbox has no browser, so WebGL/WebGPU/DOS emulation could not be launched end-to-end here. Each card states its host, technology and requirements honestly.

games.title: Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup
games.description: A deep open-source roguelike played through WebTiles on public servers — no install, no account.

games.title: Pokémon Showdown
games.description: An open-source browser battle simulator — pick a format and hit Battle! It ships no Nintendo ROMs or game assets.

games.title: Lichess
games.description: A free, ad-free, open-source chess server. Play the computer or a quick random game without signing up.

research.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops Zombies
research.reason: A WebAssembly port was briefly hosted at vel.gg. The original /bo1z address now shows 'Unavailable for legal reasons' after an Activision DMCA notice to Cloudflare on 19 Oct 2026. The site streamed Activision's own maps and assets, so no link is provided.

research.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops II (browser ports)
research.reason: Activision issued a DMCA takedown on 11 Oct 2026 because the ports used maps, models and animations exported from the retail PC game. Both multiplayer and Zombies builds were removed.

research.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (IW4L)
research.reason: A from-scratch Rust/Bevy runtime that reads the player's own MW2 install. It ships no Activision code or assets, but it is a research runtime rather than a finished game and needs your own copy.

research.title: Skate 3
research.reason: A Rust/Bevy clean-room engine compiled to WebAssembly with WebGPU. The public build explicitly asks for your own converted copy of Skate 3, so it is not 'no game files'. Needs Chrome/Edge 113+ with WebGPU.

research.title: The Simpsons: Hit & Run
research.reason: A WebAssembly port streams roughly 3.6 GB of the 2003 game's data from its own server and is reportedly built on source code leaked in 2021. Unlicensed; no link provided.

research.title: Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005)
research.reason: Browser builds stream the retail game's files from third-party servers without EA's authorisation. Not linked.

research.title: Need for Speed: Underground 2
research.reason: Unlicensed browser builds stream retail assets. No authorised browser release exists.

research.title: Grand Theft Auto V
research.reason: playgta5.com went live on 6 Oct 2026 and was taken offline within hours. Coverage says roughly 700 MB of compressed game assets were distributed, reportedly derived from leaked source.

research.title: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City (DOS Zone)
research.reason: Take-Two / Rockstar sent DOS Zone a DMCA notice in December 2025 even though the port required users to supply their own game files. Later builds removed the distributed files.

research.title: Grand Theft Auto III (re3 / browser builds)
research.reason: Open-source re3/reVC engine reimplementations need your own legitimately owned game files. Browser builds exist but are subject to the same publisher pressure as Vice City.

research.title: Cyberpunk 2077
research.reason: Listed on ported2browser.com as a work-in-progress with game-breaking bugs. Unlicensed asset distribution; no link provided.

research.title: Halo: Combat Evolved
research.reason: A decompilation-based browser build was demoed with large multiplayer matches. It is unauthorised and its availability fluctuates; the underlying work requires the original game data.

research.title: Half-Life
research.reason: Browser builds use the open-source Xash3D FWGS engine and require your own Half-Life installation; Valve has never released a browser version.

research.title: Counter-Strike 1.6
research.reason: Web builds reproduce the client but need the original game assets from a legal installation. No official browser release.

research.title: Quake III Arena
research.reason: ioquake3-derived WebAssembly builds exist, but the shareware demo / full game data must be supplied by the player. id Software has not released a browser version.

research.title: Super Mario 64
research.reason: The sm64 decomp port runs in a browser, but its creator changed it to require the player's own ROM to reduce legal exposure — the same model as the 79 ports listed below.

research.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
research.reason: Decompilation-based browser builds need the player's own ROM. No authorised browser release.

research.title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask
research.reason: Decompilation-based browser builds need the player's own ROM.

research.title: Perfect Dark
research.reason: Decompilation-based browser builds need the player's own ROM.

research.title: Diddy Kong Racing
research.reason: Decompilation-based browser builds need the player's own ROM.

research.title: Donkey Kong 64
research.reason: Decompilation-based browser builds need the player's own ROM.

research.title: Conker's Bad Fur Day
research.reason: Decompilation-based browser builds need the player's own ROM.

research.title: Tomb Raider (OpenLara)
research.reason: OpenLara is an open-source reimplementation of the classic Tomb Raider engine. Its browser demo needs the original game assets from a copy you own.

research.title: Minecraft 1.8.8 (Eaglercraft)
research.reason: An unofficial fan port of Minecraft Java 1.8.8. It is not made or endorsed by Mojang, so it is kept out of the playable collection; Minecraft Classic above is the official alternative.

research.title: Portal: The Flash Version
research.reason: A licensed-by-necessity fan-made 2D Flash-era reimagining of Portal, preserved and playable in a browser with no assets from Valve's game. Listed in the research database rather than the playable grid because the host also carries unlicensed AAA ports.

research.title: Super Mario 63
research.reason: A well-known fan-made Flash platformer, preserved for browser play. Fan game, not a Nintendo release. Listed in the research database rather than the playable grid because the host also carries unlicensed AAA ports.

research.title: Ultimate Flash Sonic
research.reason: A fan-made Flash Sonic platformer preserved for browser play. Not a Sega release. Listed in the research database rather than the playable grid because the host also carries unlicensed AAA ports.

research.title: Resident Evil 4 / Tekken 5 (ported2browser)
research.reason: Reported running in Chrome by XDA, but the host bundles copyrighted retail assets and is subject to DMCA takedowns. Not linked.

research.title: Burnout 3 / Skate / Tony Hawk
research.reason: No authorised browser version found for these franchises during this research pass.

research.title: Microsoft 3D Pinball: Space Cadet
research.reason: The Windows 95 pack-in pinball table is playable in-browser through community WebAssembly builds; no game files need to be supplied by the player. Listed in the research database rather than the playable grid because the host also carries unlicensed AAA ports.
